source_text: Ostende mihi faciem tuam; sonet vox tua in auribus meis, quoniam vox tua suavis et facies tua speciosa. Sponsus, qui saliens super montes venerat et per fenestras prospiciebat, secundo dicit: Surge, veni; nunc addit locum: in velamento petrae iuxta promurale. Promurale murus ante murum est; locus secretior, ubi velamine remoto facies ostendatur et vox audiatur.
pass_a_gloss: Show to-me face your; let-sound voice your in ears my, because voice your sweet and face your beautiful. Bridegroom, who leaping upon mountains had-come and through windows was-looking, a-second-time says: Rise, come; now adds place: in covering of-rock beside outer-wall. Outer-wall wall before wall is; place more-secret, where with-veil removed face may-be-shown and voice may-be-heard.
pass_b_english: [[Show me your face; let your voice sound in my ears, for your voice is sweet and your face is fair >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:14]]. The Bridegroom, who had come leaping on the mountains and looking through the windows, says a second time: Arise, come; now he adds the place: in the covert of the rock beside the outer wall. The outer wall is a wall before the wall — a more secret place where, the veil removed, the face may be shown and the voice heard.
